_comment: Q12 amendment 4 — the single-quarter question on OPUS. Opus does not need the rule: wx-none 9/10, wx-desc 9/9, wx-resp 10/10. Without the rule it builds a reference quarter from 4–31 prior years itself; 0 runs took the factor road. The registered prediction (both rule arms >= control + 5) is FALSIFIED. Combined with amendment 3: the rule is worth nothing on haiku (0/10 everywhere), 7/10 on sonnet, and nothing on opus (already 9/10) — the metadata effect is concentrated in the middle model on this question.
question: weather-single-quarter
model: opus (claude-opus-5 via the Agent tool's 'opus' alias)
registered: open-questions.md Q12 amendment 4, commit 2a681e8, before the run.

prediction.registered: both rule arms >= wx-none + 5, and within 2 of each other; falsified if either leads by < 3 or they differ by >= 4
prediction.verdict: FALSIFIED — no headroom on opus: the control is at ceiling.

across_models.reading: The rule helps only the middle model. haiku does not act on it; opus does not need it. research-frame's 'metadata matters most on the weakest model' does not hold for a rule that requires fetching extra data.

manual_test_corroboration: Two manual main-session runs (Opus 5.5, n=1 each) on a nine-month variant: with the rule (wx3) and without it (wx1) Opus both refused the factor and built a 2014–2023 reference. Recorded in the Q9 host-limit notes.
log_audit: harness 246 vs 225 in the log page: the page (limit 500, no offset) starts at 17:58:43Z, 33 s after the window opened, so the first rows fell off it. Not reconcilable with this tool; disclosed. 6 manual-test rows excluded by queryIntent.
caveats: opus via the Agent 'opus' alias; one question; 30 runs; 1 NO_RECORD (wx-desc wave 6) dropped, not replaced.
